'''Isaiah Jaden Collier''' (born October 8, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class.

==Early life==
Collier grew up in [[Marietta, Georgia]] and attended [[Wheeler High School (Georgia)|Wheeler High School]]. His coach at Wheeler was his uncle, Larry Thompson.<ref>{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Williams|title=How Cincinnati established itself as a finalist for Isaiah Collier|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3898339/2022/11/15/isaiah-collier-cincinnati-bearcats/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 15, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> Collier averaged 18 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, and two steals per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|title=Class 6A blog: Wheeler, Buford boys lead pack of contenders|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/high-school-sports-blog/class-6a-blog-wheeler-buford-boys-lead-pack-of-contenders/HMU7IJBDDRBRLKGYRGTYKMHSZ4/|work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He played in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) following the season and averaged 17.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 6.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Isaiah Collier Preps for Michigan Visit as Kentucky Jumps in the Mix|url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/07/22/isaiah-collier-kentucky-michigan-nike-peach-jam-2022-college-basketball-recruiting|website=[[SI.com]]|date=July 22, 2022|access-date=February 3, 2023}}</ref> Collier suffered a meniscus injury in his knee while participating in workouts with the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] in May 2022, which caused him to miss the rest of the EYBL circuit.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Justin|last1=Williams|first2=Seth|last2=Davis|first3=Tobias|last3=Bass|title=USC lands 5-star PG Isaiah Collier: Why it’s a recruiting splash for Trojans|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3903999/2022/11/16/isaiah-collier-usc-recruiting/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> He participated in the Curry Camp and was named the camp's MVP.<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Bednarowski|title=Wheeler's Collier named MVP of Curry Camp|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/wheelers-collier-named-mvp-curry-223300167.html|work=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=August 9, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref>

Collier for his senior year averaged 19.6 points, 6.8 assists, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.2 steals while shooting 52 percent from inside the arc, 38 percent from 3-point range, and 77 percent from the free throw line.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=2022-23 MaxPreps All-America Team: Cameron Boozer of Columbus headlines high school basketball's best|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/SxUDpqUOuUW4VE3APSX7fw/2022-23-maxpreps-all-america-team-cameron-boozer-of-columbus-headlines-high-school-basketballs-best.htm|website=[[MaxPreps.com]]|date=March 29, 2023|access-date=August 5, 2023}}</ref>

Collier was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Collier becomes Wheeler's sixth McDonald's All-American|url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/collier-becomes-wheelers-sixth-mcdonalds-all-american/article_e23ea244-9cdf-11ed-843a-73b72a9d6e1e.html|work=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He was also selected to play for Team USA in the [[Nike Hoops Summit]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|title=Bronny James, DJ Wagner, ‘JuJu’ Watkins headline Nike Hoop Summit rosters|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4200387/2023/02/14/bronny-james-juju-watkins-nike-hoop-summit/|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023}}</ref> Collier won the 2023 [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]] and was named [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]].<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Bednarowski|title=Wheeler's Isaiah Collier named Naismith High School Player of the Year|url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/wheelers-isaiah-collier-named-naismith-high-school-player-of-the-year/article_ec224828-9e6-11ed-bd7f-93f1dd0da993.html|work=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=March 6, 2023}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Bednarowski|title=Collier named Mr. Basketball;14 players earn All-Metro honors from ATC|url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/collier-named-mr-basketball-14-players-earn-all-metro-honors-from-atc/article_4f4cb9b6-c733-11ed-8d65-1b96a7b601ba.html|work=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|date=March 20, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}}</ref>

Collier was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, according to major recruiting services.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dan|last=McDonald|title=Five-star guard Isaiah Collier sifting through high-major offers|url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/five-star-guard-isaiah-collier-sifting-through-high-major-offers|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=December 3, 2021|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Williams|title=On Isaiah Collier and how Cincinnati is recruiting the nation’s No. 1 point guard|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3609171/2022/09/20/isaiah-collier-cincinnati-basketball/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=September 20, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He was rated as the number one overall prospect for the 2023 class by ''[[ESPN]]'' and ''[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Travis|last=Branham|title=What makes Isaiah Collier the class of 2023's newest No. 1 player|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Number-one-prospect-in-2023-basketball-recruiting-247Sports-rankings-update-Isaiah-Collier-Cincinnati-USC-UCLA-Michigan-191896711/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=August 22, 2022|access-date=February 4, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Brandon|last=Jenkins|title=Triple Threat Alert: Isaiah Collier and Dink Pate shine in big matchups|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Triple-Threat-Alert-Isaiah-Collier-ESPN-USC-Dink-Pate-Baye-Fall-Dennis-Evans-204353497/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> On November 16, 2022, Collier committed to playing college basketball for [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] after considering offers from [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Paul|last2=Biancardi|title=PG Isaiah Collier, top-10 recruit in 2023, commits to USC|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/35039682/pg-isaiah-collier-top-10-recruit-2023-commits-usc|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=USC men's basketball lands 5-star PG Isaiah Collier|url=https://www.presstelegram.com/2022/11/16/isaiah-collier-nations-top-recruit-commits-to-usc-mens-basketball/|work=[[The Press-Telegram]]|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=February 4, ==College career==
Collier enrolled at the [[University of Southern California]] in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|first=Erik|last=McKinney|title=USC Freshman and Nation's No. 1 Recruit Isaiah Collier to Wear a Fitting Jersey Number|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/usc-trojans/news/usc-freshman-and-nations-no-1-recruit-isaiah-collier-to-wear-a-fitting-jersey-number/|website=On3.com|date=June 26, 2023|access-date=June 28, 2023}}</ref> He started the Trojans' season opener against [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and scored 18 points with three rebounds and six assists before fouling out of the game.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Paul|last1=Gutierrez|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|first3=John|last3=Gasaway|first4=Myron|last4=Medcalf|title=2023-24 men's college basketball opening day overreactions|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38833741/overreactions-takeaways-observations-2023-24-men-college-basketball-opening-day|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 7, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}}</ref>

Collier averaged 16.3 points, 4.3 assists and 1.5 steals per game. On April 10, 2024, Collier declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|author=Adrian Wojnarowski|title=Isaiah Collier headed to NBA draft after freshman season at USC|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39914681/isaiah-collier-headed-nba-draft-freshman-season-usc|website=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2024|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 26, 2024, Collier was selected with the 29th overall pick by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Reynolds|title=Why the Utah Jazz waited for USC’s Isaiah Collier to fall to them in the NBA Draft|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2024/06/26/uscs-isaiah-collier-falls-utah/|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> and on July 2, he signed with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Cody Williams and Isaiah Collier|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-cody-williams-and-isaiah-collier|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Salt Lake City Stars Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Salt-Lake-City-Stars/42/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}}</ref>

On January 26, 2025, Collier was named the starting point guard in place of [[Keyonte George]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz lose to Bucks, but say moving Collier to a starter is 'best for team' right now|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51238922/jazz-lose-to-bucks-but-say-moving-collier-to-a-starter-is-best-for-team-right-now|access-date=January 27, 2025|website=ksl.com|language=en}}</ref> On February 8, Collier set a new Jazz rookie record for assists in a half, totaling 10 in the first half against the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sports |first=CHANDLER HOLT KSL |date=February 7, 2025 |title=Isaiah Collier Sets Jazz History In First Half Against Suns |url=https://kslsports.com/nba/utah-jazz/isaiah-collier-jazz-record/538194 |access-date=March 1, 2025 |website=KSL Sports |language=en-us}}</ref> On February 28, Collier recorded a career-high 14 assists in a 117–116 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705424|title=Walker Kessler's late dunk lifts Jazz to 117-116 win over short-handed Timberwolves|website=ESPN|date=March 1, 2025|access-date=March 31, 2025}}</ref> He was named February's [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] Rookie of the Month after averaging 11.5 points, 9.5 assists and 3.9 rebounds per month.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Monthly NBA Awards: Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley win honors for Feb. {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/monthly-nba-awards-february-2025 |access-date=March 17, 2025 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> On March 31, in a game against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Collier surpassed [[John Stockton]]'s previous record of 415 for the most assists recorded in a season by a rookie in Jazz franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-utah-rookie-breaks-john-stockton-bonkers-assist-record-hornets-game|title=Jazz rookie breaks John Stockton's bonkers assist record in Hornets game|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=March 31, 2025|access-date=March 31, 2025}}</ref>

On February 3, 2026, Collier recorded a career-high 22 assists in a 131–122 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]], the most assists in a game by a player in Jazz franchise history since John Stockton in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 3, 2026 |title=Isaiah Collier has career-high 22 assists as Jazz beat Pacers 131-122 with 7 players |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810572 |access-date=February 3, 2026 |website=[[ESPN|ESPN.com]]}}</ref>
